div.head: ECf 32 B 7
div.ab: Et qui leges apostabit, si fuerit Anglicus uel Dacus uel Waliscus uel Albanicus aut Insulicola, were sue reus sit erga regem. Et si secundo id faciat, reddat bis weram suam. Et si quid addat tertio, reus sit omnium que habebit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 657 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 B …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
Liebermann prints the words borrowed from Quadr. II Cn. 83–83, 2 in smaller type; his margin names the source (Quadr. II Cn. 83. 83, 1; 2).

note.seg: ähnlich interpolirt der Londoner Wl art. retr. 1; vgl. u. S. 660**
the Londoner interpolates similarly at Wl art. retr. 1; cf. below, p. 660**

div.ab: And whoever casts aside the laws, whether he be English or Dane or Welsh or Scot or Islander, let him be liable to the king for his wergild. And if he does it a second time, let him pay his wergild twice. And if he adds anything a third time, let him be liable for all that he has.
